reading-the-book-curing-ulsquire.text: Ah, excellent, you've made your own serum and it seems to work well! Many thanks for using the Serum on me! But beware, I may start to change back soon!

options.text: Who are you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: My name is Ulsquire Shauncy, I'm the local teacher and priest around here. You've really come at a time when  Mort'ton is in a terrible state.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The emanations from the rest of Morytania affect the people here terribly turning them into mindless creatures. And, as if that wasn't enough, we get picked off by the evil Shades that exist in this area.

steps.player: Wow, you guys seem to be really at the bottom of the food chain around here.

options.text: What is this place?

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: This sad and afflicted little town is called 'Mort'ton'. In it's heyday it was a busy and bustling market town with a speciality for interring the dead.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The vile emanations from the Sanguinesti area started to spread and the town hasn't been the same since. The serum you made was the one that Herbi Flax was working on. Unfortunately the serum isn't permanent.

steps.player: Do you know how I could make the serum permanent?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I remember Herbi Flax talking about the serum. He said it worked on what he called the 'biological' effects of the affliction but that some other secondary effect was at work which he didn't quite understand.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: He was interested in 'Flaemtaer', the ruined temple to the North. I found this odd. A man of science studying a structure dedicated to faith and the struggle of good verus evil, another concept he didn't understand.

options.text: What's going on around here?

steps.player: What's going on around here?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The people are affected by the emanations from  the rest of Morytania and the dead from the tombs  have manifested into shadow creatures.

options.text: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.player: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: They are the disturbed spirits of those interred in the earth beneath Mort'ton. Their eternal spirits have been poisoned by the close vicinity to the evil nature of the inhabitants of the Sanguinesti area.

options.text: Is there anyone else worth talking to around here?

steps.player: Is there anyone else worth talking to around here?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Well, there's my good friend Razmire Keelgan. He's a prominent shop owner in Mort'ton, at least he was before he was affected by the area.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I know he tried to gather the militia together to fight the shades. He might know something about the temple. Razmire lives in the building to the west just over there, go and talk to him.

steps.text: My name is Razmire Keelgan, I run a couple of shops in Mort'ton but don't get much custom these days.

steps.player: Which stores do you run?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: I run a general store with a few useful items, and I have a building supplies store, I'm hoping that when things get better down here, people will want to buy items to repair their buildings.

steps.text: Well to be honest, all of my stock is packed away right now seeing as the town is all overrun with these Shades. I tell you what. You put an end to five Shades for me and I'll open the store for you!

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: I have details on that dilapidated temple to the North. These shades have a purpose - they jealously guard their burial treasure! If you can do me some favours, I could help you to locate it!

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: This place is called Mort'ton, it used to be a quiet town with a specialism in death. That is to say that many burial tombs were created here in the naturally formed caves under this very village.

options.text: What's going on around here?

steps.player: What's going on around here?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Well, the people of the village, my usual customers... are all affected by the emanations from some place to the North East. Ulsquire can give you the name.

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Needless to say Herbi was working on a serum to help us and you stumbled across the recipe! I for one am grateful to you, but there's a lot left to do before Mort'ton is returned to it's former glory.

options.text: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.player: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Those disgusting entities are the filth that have ruined my life. They're the restless spirits of the dead who jealously guard their burial treasure yet feed on the  life force of the living.

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: I've heard that they jealously guard their tomb treasure and that it's worth plundering. I need you to kill five shades and bring me their remains so that I can conduct some experiments. Will you do it?

options.text: Yes, I'll dispatch those dark and evil creatures.

steps.player: Yes, I'll dispatch those dark and evil creatures.

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Great, that's what I wanted to hear. When you've done it, bring back all the remains,  I want to inspect them.

options.text: Sorry, not right now, I need to do something else first.

steps.text: Ok, fair enough...

steps.text: It's ancient and has been desecrated since before I was born. I've always felt that it was quite a nice place to sit and have a picnic, quite a nice view out of the swamps of Mort Myre.

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: I told Ulsquire that if he can afford to go half's  with me on the building materials, I'd help him to  try and fix it up one day. I've always wondered  what it looked like back in pagan times.

talking-with-ulsquire-again.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
talking-with-ulsquire-again.text: Ah, hello again, what can I do for you now?

options.text: What did you find out about the remains?

steps.player: What did you find out about the remains.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The shade remains are made of a strange substance  which I've not come across before. I believe we should put these tormented spirits to rest.

steps.player: How can we do that? You can't even bury the remains!

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Quite right...I was thinking that a holy cremation would do the trick, but the funeral pyres need specially prepared 'pyre logs' - normal logs that have been  treated with 'sacred oil' to give it a nice holy touch.

steps.player: How would I make some sacred oil?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: You won't! It's a pagan secret lost a long time ago. Normally I would try to bless some commonly found vegetable oil, but I'm so weak from this illness that I know I just won't be able to do it.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Huh! I used to joke with Herbi Flax that if 'Flaemtaer temple' was still standing, we could practice some ancient pagan rituals and incite the sacred flame! Huh, I'm not surprised that he never took me seriously!

options.text: What can you tell me about that temple?

steps.player: What can you tell me about that temple?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Hmm, interesting question. It is an ancient pagan  temple referred to as Flaemtaer. I've studied it quite    a lot, one day I hope to be able to rebuild it, who knows what ancient power it could unleash?

steps.player: How can you rebuild a totally destroyed temple?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I couldn't do it alone, I'd need a few expert artisans to help with the construction. I'd also need a good supply of limestone bricks, swamp paste and timber beams. Thankfully Razmire stocks all these items. (Sigh)

options.text: Do you know how I could make this serum permanent?

steps.player: Do you know how I could make this serum permanent?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The serum is a product of science. Herbi was a clever man to have made it, but he didn't integrate anything from the spiritual world into his work - and for all of his hard science there is still something missing.

steps.player: So, you don't know then!

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I'm a man of faith...that's all I know. Sometimes I feel that we should experiment with the sacred and the holy, not just the crude matter we find around us everyday.

options.text: What should I do now?

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: That's up to you my friend! I once heard someone say that making your own decisions is the only real freedom you have. Exercise your freedom my friend,  while you still can.

options.text: Ok, thanks

steps.text: I've researched this much, it seems that the temple was dedicated to the worship of elemental flame or fire. The sacred flame was said to be very holy and was used somehow to sanctify oil for use in cremations.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy

olive oil (3)

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I'm not surprised. The temple represents holiness. They may feel that it has power over them in some way. My advice is to carry on and finish the temple if you can, and see what happens. You may need help though!

steps.player: How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: You may need help building the temple or defending yourself against the Shades. I'm sure if you ask around nicely you would be able to get some help.

options.text: Tell me more about the Shades.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Shades.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: All undead hate mortal spirituality. It's a symbol of mortal hope in the face of death and the unknown. The temple represents the finality of true death where all ties to the mortal world are lost.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The Shades wish to forever possess the value of their tomb treasures and jealously guard them in death as they did in life. They are afraid of true death and so try to destroy anything which reminds them of it.
